pr.title: Suggest {to,from}_ne_bytes for transmutations between arrays and integers, etc
pr.author: bend-n

classification.name: CheckUnnecessaryTransmutes
evidence: The PR's core change is a new MIR lint pass. The new file defines `CheckUnnecessaryTransmutes` with a concrete `impl<'tcx> crate::MirLint<'tcx> for CheckUnnecessaryTransmutes`, and lib.rs both declares it in `declare_passes!` and registers it in the `mir_built` MIR-level lint list. The remaining changes (std allow attributes, test updates, doc examples, submodule bump, formatting) support this lint and are not separate passes, so only this pass is assigned.

processing.reason: The only historically risky replacement that can change behavior is `u8 -> bool` becoming `(arg == 1)`. It differs from `transmute` only for bytes other than 0 or 1 (e.g. 2 or 255), but those original transmutes produce an invalid `bool` and are UB under Miri. On all defined inputs (0 and 1) the replacement gives the same result. All other suggested rewrites (`from_ne_bytes`/`to_ne_bytes`, `cast_signed`/`cast_unsigned`, `from_bits`/`to_bits`, `char` conversions, `bool as integer`, `char::from_u32_unchecked`) preserve the original behavior for valid inputs; mismatched array/integer widths are already rejected by `transmute`'s size requirement. Thus there is no source-grounded pair where both the original and transformed functions pass Miri and produce different defined values. A test using `transmute(2u8)` would demonstrate UB-to-defined change only, not a valid defined-execution counterexample.

analysis.summary: This PR introduces the MIR lint pass `CheckUnnecessaryTransmutes` (lint `unnecessary_transmutes`), registered in the `mir_built` lint list. It visits call terminators, recognizes the `transmute` intrinsic with exactly one argument, and matches the input/output types to suggest a std method (`from_ne_bytes`/`to_ne_bytes`, `cast_signed`/`cast_unsigned`, `from_bits`/`to_bits`, `char` conversions, `bool` casts, and `u8 -> bool`). The lint emits a `MachineApplicable` source suggestion plus optional help; it does not rewrite MIR.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR there was no `unnecessary_transmutes` lint: transmute calls between primitive/array/`char`/`bool` types were not flagged as having safer standard-library alternatives. The new visitor only examines `TerminatorKind::Call { func, args, .. }`, checks `self.tcx.is_intrinsic(func_def_id, sym::transmute)`, extracts the single argument snippet, and dispatches on `(input.kind(), fn_sig.output().kind())`. Examples: `[u8; _] => uint/float/int` suggests `{output}::from_ne_bytes({arg})`; the reverse suggests `{input}::to_ne_bytes({arg})`; `char -> u32` suggests `u32::from`; `u32 -> char` suggests `char::from_u32_unchecked`; `uNN <-> iNN` uses `cast_signed`/`cast_unsigned`; `fNN <-> uNN` uses `to_bits`/`from_bits`; `bool -> integer` uses `(arg) as T`; `u8 -> bool` uses `(arg == 1)`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: This is a lint-introduction PR, not a bug-fix PR, and the pass performs no MIR rewrite. The only transformation is the diagnostic's machine-applicable source substitution. Its correctness invariant is that the replacement must preserve the original transmute's behavior for all defined inputs (and must not make previously-UB inputs unsound). The historically risky suggested transformations are: `u8 -> bool` becomes `(arg == 1)`, which maps bytes other than 0/1 (e.g. 2) to `false`, whereas transmuting such a byte to `bool` is UB/invalid; and `u32 -> char` becomes `char::from_u32_unchecked(arg)`, which retains the same validity precondition and only mentions `char::from_u32(…).unwrap()` in help. The pass deliberately does not validate array length: "dont check the length; transmute does that for us." The visitor also uses `span_to_snippet(arg).expect("ok")`, so a robust replacement must not assume every MIR argument span has retrievable source text (macro-generated spans can lack snippets).
analysis.inputDomain: MIR call terminators in any body linted at `mir_built` (including const/static initializers), where the callee resolves to the `transmute` intrinsic and has exactly one input argument. Matching type pairs are: `[u8; N]` to integer/float primitives and back; `char` to/from `u32`; unsigned integer to signed integer of the same family; signed integer to unsigned integer; float to unsigned integer; unsigned integer to float; `bool` to any integer; and unsigned integer to `bool` (the code pattern is `Uint(_)`, but tests only exercise `u8`).
analysis.trigger: A call terminator whose callee is the `transmute` intrinsic, with a single argument, and whose input/output types match one of the lint's supported primitive/array/`char`/`bool` pairs.
preconditions: The terminator is `TerminatorKind::Call { func, args, .. }` with exactly one `Spanned` argument: `let [Spanned { span: arg, .. }] = **args`.
The callee signature has exactly one input: `let [input] = fn_sig.inputs() else { return None };`.
The `(input.kind(), fn_sig.output().kind())` pair matches a supported arm; unmatched pairs return `None`.
The argument source snippet is obtainable via `span_to_snippet(arg).expect("ok")`.
The terminator scope yields a lint root: `terminator.source_info.scope.lint_root(&self.body.source_scopes)`.
For the suggestion to compile, the array length must equal the integer/float byte width; the lint itself does not check length.
pitfalls: Do not add an array-length check to gate `from_ne_bytes`/`to_ne_bytes` without preserving the comment's rationale: the pass intentionally relies on transmute's size requirement rather than checking the length itself.

`u8 -> bool` is only matched for `Uint(_)`; `i8 -> bool` is intentionally not linted. The regression test contains `let z: bool = transmute(1i8); // no error!`, so broadening the match would change expected diagnostics.
`u8 -> bool` as `(arg == 1)` is not behavior-preserving for invalid bytes: `transmute(2u8)` is invalid bool, while `2u8 == 1` is defined `false`. The PR itself labels this case "(debatable)".
`u32 -> char` suggests `char::from_u32_unchecked`, which keeps the caller's validity obligation; `char::from_u32(…).unwrap()` appears only as help, not as the replacement.

`bool -> integer` uses `(arg) as T`, not `T::from(arg)`, even though the PR description mentions `from`; the code arm is `(Bool, Int(..) | Uint(..)) => err(format!("({arg}) as {}", fn_sig.output()))`.
The suggestion embeds the original argument snippet in parentheses, hence the test's `#![allow(unused_parens)]`; rewrites such as `(z) as u8` are expected.
`span_to_snippet(arg).expect("ok")` can panic if the argument has no source snippet; use a fallible snippet path when handling macro-generated code.

Because the lint runs at `mir_built`, it also fires in const/static bodies that later fail const evaluation; many existing const and Miri tests had to add `#![allow(unnecessary_transmutes)]` to retain their original diagnostic focus.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a Rust UI `run-rustfix` test with `#![deny(unnecessary_transmutes)]` covering both directions of each supported pair and asserting the `.fixed` output. The historical test `tests/ui/transmute/unnecessary-transmutation.rs` does this for `[u8; N] -> uN/iN/fN` and back, `char <-> u32`, `iN <-> uN` via casts, `uN <-> fN` via bits, `bool <-> u8`, and includes the negative case `let z: bool = transmute(1i8); // no error!`. Include additional boundary-value tests for `u8 -> bool` (0, 1, 2) if checking behavior instead of only diagnostics, and test macro-generated transmute arguments to exercise snippet retrieval. For byte conversions, test only equal-width arrays so the suggested `from_ne_bytes`/`to_ne_bytes` remains compilable. Confirm the lint is silent for unsupported pairs and that the suggested replacement compiles under the same unsafe/const context.
